text: Welcome to RFC Legends, built at ETHGlobal Tokyo twenty twenty-six: an idle rooster adventure whose birds carry farm-signed records onchain. Here's where it comes from, how it works, and what we built for World, ENS and Curvegrid.

RFC began at Ninlanee Farm in Thailand, which raises Thai fighting roosters. The dream: new universal rules that turn Thai cockfighting into an international sport, the way ONE Championship did for Muay Thai.

From the farm grew the RFC Club app, RFC TV and our media channels. Coming soon is RFC NFT, a real-world asset that maps each farm rooster onchain for digital sales. And RFC's AI scoring aims to judge results to one fair standard.

RFC Legends is the game for RFC NFT holders. Live today: an idle adventure with your rooster, rare drops, guild chat, a shared guild boss, and a market to trade drops. Next come holder privileges, breeding, and dressing up your rooster and trainer.

A server-authoritative TypeScript engine runs every combat tick and settles offline rewards, with PocketBase holding player state, guild chat and the guild boss. Five contracts on Sepolia hold rare items and rooster records, while World ID, ENS version two and MultiBaas handle proof of human, pedigree and indexing.

In the demo loop, a boss drops a rare card, the player proves they're human with World ID, and a server-signed EIP-712 voucher mints it as an ERC-1155 item. A buyer pays in the Rare Market, and the contract splits ninety-ten between seller and treasury in one transaction. Then we show two refusals, an unverified bot and a second wallet of the same human.

For World, IDKit gates the whole economy. Our server verifies each proof with the signal pinned to the player's wallet and a one-time nonce, so it can't be replayed. The nullifier is bound to one wallet and mirrored onchain in HumanRegistry, which the mint and the market both check before any value moves.

Our first IDKit line to a live verify took sixty-two minutes. The blockers: an undocumented staging token, a simulator that ignored our connect link, and a single simulator identity worldwide. Our top request: let the Portal reject a reused nullifier per action, and check the signal a proof was made for.

For ENS, the name is the pedigree. Offspring are subnames inside their sire's own registry, so chick zero one dot theprawang is its sire's child onchain. A permissioned resolver lets only the farm's key write health records, while the namespace owner handles bloodline fields. Our rooster pages resolve it all live.

For Curvegrid, every rooster token needs two parties: the issuer submits the mint, and the farm co-signs the leg-ring ID, bloodline and hatch date. The farm also signs health attestations anyone can relay onchain. All five contracts are indexed in MultiBaas, and the ninety-ten sale history comes from a saved Sold-event query.

Everything onchain was written during ETHGlobal Tokyo: five contracts verified on Etherscan and Sourcify, a hundred and five Foundry tests at one hundred percent line coverage, and a live Sepolia demo. World ID work started at seven thirty-seven UTC on day one, and MultiBaas indexing was wired up during the event.
That's RFC Legends. Play it now at rfclegends dot rfcclub dot app, and find every contract, pointer and transaction in our GitHub repo. Thank you World, ENS and Curvegrid, and thanks for watching!
